quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always use your headlight when riding.
Wave your arms.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight when riding.
questions.explanation: To be more visible at an intersection, use your headlight and position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around you so you can avoid hazards. Do not count on eye contact alone to make drivers notice you.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
Stays in the same part of the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to become more visible.
Only rides on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider has three lane position choices. Choose the safest position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When using a sidecar to carry a load, you should:

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load loose in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure all loads in a sidecar so they do not move and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place loads toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Give you a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that lets you see others and lets them see you. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot for long periods.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Always press the left handgrip.
Always press the right handgrip.
Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean that way.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Is not serious.
Takes away your ability to change direction.
Usually fixes itself.
Is only dangerous if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes away your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the rear wheel locks, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of the motorcycle's stopping power.
Provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's stopping power.
Should only be used on wet roads.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's stopping power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks, you will:

options.text: Have a sudden increase in power to the rear wheel.
Have a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
Have a sudden loss of power to the front wheel.
Have a sudden increase in power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt breaks, you will lose power to the rear wheel immediately.

questions.question: To be seen in the rearview mirror of the car ahead, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.
Weave back and forth in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When following a car, the driver will most likely see you if you stay in the center of your lane behind them. This puts you in their rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before riding. Have them get on only after you start the engine. They should sit close to you without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To see better when passing a vehicle on the left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane
In the right portion of your lane
In the center portion of your lane
Try to stand up on your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see better and makes oncoming traffic more likely to see you.

questions.question: What headlight should you use when riding in fog?

options.text: Your high beam
Your low beam
No lights
Alternate between low and high beams

questions.correctAnswerText: Your low beam
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble
Use the brakes slowly
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle
Downshift

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when your motorcycle wobbles. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do when braking?

options.text: Start slowing sooner than usual
Start slowing later than usual
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly
Brake softer than usual to protect the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing sooner than usual
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds extra weight. Your motorcycle will need more distance to stop. Start slowing sooner than you normally would.

questions.question: When you brake, which brakes should you use?

options.text: The front brake only
The rear brake only
Both the front and rear brakes
Either front or rear, but not both

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do if you are riding next to another vehicle?

options.text: Speed up or slow down
Wave at the other driver
Stay alongside until the next exit
Let the other driver handle it

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears. Either speed up or drop back.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly
Shift your weight toward the good tire
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road
Relax your grip on the handlebars

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep your motorcycle straight. Gradually brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding
When you are slowing where drivers won't expect it
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your turn signals are not working

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are slowing where drivers won't expect it
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than larger vehicles' brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing where drivers won't expect it, such as in the middle of a block or when approaching an alley.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake provide on a motorcycle?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
About 95 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
You stop sooner than expected.
Your tire pops.
It takes longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, your wheels may lose grip and you could crash.

questions.question: On a motorcycle with a sidecar, where should the passenger sit?

options.text: On the motorcycle seat.
In the sidecar.
Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Anywhere except the motorcycle or sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the sidecar.
questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.
Next to the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves just behind the leader. This way, more experienced riders behind them can watch and help them.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT check on your tires?

options.text: Air pressure.
Tread.
General wear.
Flexibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, general wear, and tread. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: Why is riding directly next to another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may miss a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.
